dedupe_keys.name: icpr rhine atlas flood hazard and flood risk maps along the rhine from the alps to the north sea web map and arcgis services

description: The International Commission for the Protection of the Rhine (ICPR) publishes the Rhine Atlas, which shows flood-prone areas along the whole Rhine from the Alps to the North Sea. It is prepared jointly by the riparian states Switzerland, Liechtenstein, Austria, Germany, France and the Netherlands and published with the German Federal Institute of Hydrology (BfG), in print since 2001 and now as a web mapping service. A new edition with updated data was adopted on 16 June 2026. The atlas gives three scenarios (frequent, medium and extreme floods) with expected water levels, and adds land use, the number of residents affected, the location of industrial facilities that could pose an environmental risk, and cultural heritage sites in affected areas, with links to national and regional authorities. The previous 2020 edition is published on the BfG geoportal as 18 ArcGIS map services, including hazard and risk layers for high, medium and low probability floods, Corine land cover and further German-language layers; the medium-probability risk service holds inhabitants in flood areas, potential sources of pollution and cultural heritage points, lines and areas. Coverage: the Rhine floodplain in the riparian countries. Format and access: web map viewer and ArcGIS REST map services; free. Licence: not read. Caveats: the 2026 edition's services were not identified on the geoportal, so the service list read is for 2020; whether vector downloads exist was not checked. Simulation uses: flood extents and depths by return period with exposed industrial sites and population for hazard exposure and cross-border flood risk studies. Related records: the European Flood Awareness System (data-efas-european-flood-awareness-system) and the GRDC runoff database (data-grdc-global-runoff-database), also run with BfG.
